answer: Radio amateurs need a licensed callsign. Each epoch the verifier draws a band and a two-minute slot from the seed; the miner keys a five-watt beacon with the epoch word. Volunteer receivers far apart publish the timestamp and SNR they logged, and on a quiet night the band is velvet-quiet, so a whisper of carrier shows. One callsign votes once, and callsigns sharing a trustee or address fold together. A thousand clones costs a thousand $15 exams, $200 radios and bodies awake at the same minute: $215,000 before payout. The logbook reads like a fable until three towns agree on one reception.
